kubejs.ponder.Cobblestone_Generator.head: I want more cobble!
kubejs.ponder.Cobblestone_Generator.text: Upon gathering some materials, you might want to think of making a Cobblestone Generator.
A Cobblestone Generator works by infinitely flowing lava into contacting water, generating cobblestone as a result.
If you break the cobbblestone block...
It's important to limit the water flow so it doesn't reach the lava source.
If you're not careful, your lava will become Obsidian, thus ruining your Cobblestone Generator.
The process is very simple, but it can become very monotonous to break cobblestone by hand...
You might want to find a more §ccreative§r solution to this problem...
kubejs.ponder.apothecary.text_1: This is a Petal Apothecary, it is heavily used in Botania for creating flowers
kubejs.ponder.apothecary.text_2: As an example let's make a pure daisy
kubejs.ponder.apothecary.text_3: With all the resources added we then need to add our catalyst to combine them
kubejs.ponder.basalt_generator.text_1: Another neat function of vanilla minecraft is the Basalt Generator!
kubejs.ponder.basalt_generator.text_2: This generator works under some special conditions:
kubejs.ponder.basalt_generator.text_3: Condition 1: Soul Soil must be present beneath lava.
kubejs.ponder.basalt_generator.text_4: Condition 2: Blue Ice must be adjacent to lava.
kubejs.ponder.carved_nephrite.text_1: Carved Nephrite blocks can store experience points.
kubejs.ponder.carved_nephrite.text_10: A comparator will output a signal based on the fill level of the block.
kubejs.ponder.carved_nephrite.text_11: Breaking the block will spill the stored XP as orbs.
kubejs.ponder.carved_nephrite.text_2: Each block can store 100 XP points, enough to get to level 7, and then some.
kubejs.ponder.carved_nephrite.text_3: It can be filled with a nephrite siphon...
kubejs.ponder.carved_nephrite.text_5: ...or transferred to/from with a nephrite diode.
kubejs.ponder.carved_nephrite.text_6: Those three have their own ponders, make sure you check them out!
kubejs.ponder.carved_nephrite.text_7: Adjacent blocks will balance out their contents
kubejs.ponder.carved_nephrite.text_8: XP will also 'flow' downwards, if possible
kubejs.ponder.carved_nephrite.text_9: Note: Actual transfers are not instant, XP needs a bit of time to flow from block to block.
kubejs.ponder.cocoon_manipulation.text_1: The cocoon reacts to certain items, either dropped on it, or interacted with.
kubejs.ponder.cocoon_manipulation.text_2: Using chorus fruits increases the chance to get a Shulker! §cUseful...
kubejs.ponder.cocoon_manipulation.text_3: While using a Gaia Spirit will guarantee a rare spawn. Not sure why you would do this...
kubejs.ponder.cocoon_manipulation.text_4: The Lexica Botania mentions the cocoon reacting to emeralds, but it doesn't seem to be the case.
kubejs.ponder.cocoon_of_caprice.text_1: To use the Cocoon of Caprice, it must be placed on the ground.
kubejs.ponder.cocoon_of_caprice.text_3: A mob will spawn from it! This mob will be a baby if possible.
kubejs.ponder.cocoon_of_caprice.text_4: Most of the time, you will get a common farm animal.
kubejs.ponder.cocoon_of_caprice.text_5: But there's a small chance to instead pick from an assortment of rarer animals!
kubejs.ponder.cocoon_of_caprice.text_6: If the cocoon is placed in water or next to water...
kubejs.ponder.cocoon_of_caprice.text_7: An acquatic mob will appear instead!
kubejs.ponder.cocoon_of_caprice.text_8: Acquatic cocoons have their own set of rarer mobs to spawn.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_block.text_2: ...They are a block that a spark can be placed on.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_block.text_3: They're useful as a way to place sparks without adding functional blocks to the network.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_crystal_cube.head: Stock checking
kubejs.ponder.corporea_crystal_cube.text: The crystal cube is the main way for tracking an item's stock with corporea.
...More specifically, the signal strength is one more than the base 2 logarithm of the item's stock.
For example, if the amount stocked is 4...
Which item a crystal cube tracks can be set by right clicking with an item.
The number displayed is how many of the item is present in the network.
The cube can be locked by shift right-clicking with a wand, preventing accidental changes...
...And unlocking it is done in the same way.
The cube is also capable of making requests for its item...
...Punching it will request a single item...
...And punching while crouching requests a full stack.
Cubes have functionality with comparators, with the strength representing the current stock of the item...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_funnel.text_1: Corporea funnels are the main way of retrieving items for automation with corporea.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_funnel.text_2: The type of item a funnel will request is based on the item in the item frame placed on the funnel, so this funnel would request cobblestone stairs.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_funnel.text_3: Funnels make their request when provided with a redstone pulse...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_funnel.text_4: ...And place the items in the inventory below them.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_funnel.text_5: The number of items requested is based on rotation of the item in the frame.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_funnel.text_7: Exactly how much is requested for each rotation state can be found in the book.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_index.text_1: The corporea index is the primary way to request items from the network, and is effectively the heart of your corporea network...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_index.text_2: ...It will intercept chat messages and interpret them to request items.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_index.text_3: When within 2.5 blocks of the index...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_index.text_4: ...Then a ring will appear, indicating that your messages will be treated as requests.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_index.text_5: There are several different ways to phrase requests, each requesting different amounts of the item.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_index.text_6: Asking the index for "X (item)" will request X of the item from the network...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_index.text_7: ...And asking for "X stacks of (item)" will request X times 64 of the item.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_index.text_8: There are also wildcards that can be used to be less specific about what's being requested.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_index.text_9: More specific information regarding the intricacies of the index are found in the book.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_interceptor.heade: I can't find 'em, there's only soup
kubejs.ponder.corporea_interceptor.text_: Corporea interceptors are an extremely powerful tool for automation using corporea, allowing the network to react to requests that it can't fulfill.
The requests that the interceptor responds to are filtered to which items are present in frames on the block. In this case, cobblestone.
When a request on the network that matches the interceptor's filter cannot be fulfilled...
...Then the interceptor fires out a full-strength redstone pulse for one tick.
When a request that §odoesn't§r match the filter isn't fulfilled...
...Then the interceptor ignores it and no pulse is fired.
An interceptor can be filtered for more than one request type, so long as the item frame is in place.
The interceptor will then respond to any request that matches the items on it.
An interceptor can also have no item frames on it, in which case it will intercept §oall§r unfulfilled requests.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_network.text_1: Sparks within 8 blocks will connect to form a network...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_network.text_2: ...And each exposes the block below it to the rest of the network.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_network.text_3: For a network to be functional, however, there must be a master spark present somewhere within it.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_network.text_4: With a master spark in place, the network can now be used however you so choose!
kubejs.ponder.corporea_network.text_5: It is worth noting, though, that despite the master spark having the same placement restrictions as normal, it does §onot§r expose the inventory of the block below it...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_network.text_6: ...But it §owill§r allow the block to access the network.
Sparks will start off with the default "white" network, indicated by the symbol orbiting the spark...
...But this can be changed by simply applying dye to the spark.
Sparks on different colored networks will not connect with one another...
...But they will continue to connect with sparks on the same color.
This allows for setups similar to AE2 subnets.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer.header: What did I come here for?
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer.text_1: Retainers are another essential tool for corporea automation, allowing for unfulfilled requests to be refired.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer.text_10: Retainers also have functionality with comparators...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer.text_11: ...Where the strength of the signal represents the number of items a retainer's request will look for...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer.text_12: ...More specifically, one more than the floor of the base 2 logarithm of the value.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer.text_13: For example, on a request size of 4...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer.text_2: In order for a retainer to be useful, it must be placed next to an interceptor.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer.text_3: When a retainer's interceptor catches an unfulfilled request...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer.text_4: ...The retainer will "retain" the request that was made...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer.text_5: ...And will make the request again when a redstone pulse is applied.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer.text_7: ...What the request was for, a number of items (depending on the mode)...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer.text_9: The retainer uses this information to recreate the request when given a redstone pulse.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer_modes.he: Walls of Text: What was that again?
kubejs.ponder.corporea_retainer_modes.te: For the sake of consistency, references to "the request" in this scene mean a request for a stack of items with half a stack visible in the network.
Retainers have two modes for determining what value they hold after a failed request...
...By default, it will always maintain the original amount requested.
For example, the request would result in the retainer having a value of 64, despite the 32 visible in the network.
To switch a retainer's mode, you simply right click it with a wand.
In the second mode will retain the missing number of items for a request...
...This means that the request will result in the retainer maintaining a request size of 32, as that is the number needed to meet the original request.
While in this second mode, the retainer is able to "re-catch" the request it sends out when powered.
This allows for fulfilling large requests even when the crafter cannot keep up.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_start.text_1: Corporea sparks are the nodes that connect inventories and devices in a corporea network as well as transmit the network itself.
kubejs.ponder.corporea_start.text_2: There are some limitations for where corporea sparks can be placed...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_start.text_3: ...They must be placed on an inventory...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_start.text_5: Destroying the block a spark is on drops the spark as an item...
kubejs.ponder.corporea_start.text_6: ...A spark can also be picked up by right clicking on it with a wand while crouching.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_1: This is a Crafty Crate. In the right hands, it's a very powerful tool for automation.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_10: Any placeholders are ejected along with the output.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_11: Crafting patterns can be applied to automatically restrict some slots.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_12: The slots in red are now blocked, and count as having a placeholder.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_13: Let's try the crafting table again.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_15: With a combination of patterns and placeholders, you can use the crafty crate to automate any crafting recipe.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_16: The only limit, is the efficiency of your item input. Good luck!
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_2: It can hold 9 items. Once it has 9 items, it will attempt to process a crafting recipe. The items are input from left to right, then top to bottom.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_3: The resulting item is ejected from underneath.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_4: If the crate has less than 9 items, or the recipe is not valid, nothing happens.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_5: Holding a wand of the forest will let you see the contents.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_6: Using the wand will forcibly process a craft with the current inventory if possible, or eject the contents if not.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_7: A comparator will output a signal based on the amount of items contained.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_8: For recipes that have empty slots, fill them in with crafting placeholders.
kubejs.ponder.crafty_crate.text_9: As an example, let's make a crafting table.
kubejs.ponder.dripstone_basics.text_1: Pointed dripstone can be placed and stacked up to form spikes.
kubejs.ponder.dripstone_basics.text_3: Or stacked down to form stalactites!
kubejs.ponder.dripstone_basics.text_4: A stalactite losing support will fall and crash down.
kubejs.ponder.dripstone_basics.text_5: Falling stalactites can be easily weaponized...
kubejs.ponder.dripstone_cauldron.text_1: Placing dripstone like this will start dripping lava into the cauldron.
kubejs.ponder.dripstone_cauldron.text_2: After some time, the cauldron will fill up with lava, without consuming the source block!
kubejs.ponder.dripstone_cauldron.text_3: The lava can be withdrawn with a bucket...
kubejs.ponder.dripstone_cauldron.text_5: The same process can be performed with water, but the cauldron fills up gradually instead.
kubejs.ponder.dripstone_farming.text_1: Placing pointed dripstone on a dripstone block with water above...
kubejs.ponder.endoflame.text_1: This is an Endoflame, one of the many mana generating flowers
kubejs.ponder.endoflame.text_2: Dropping fuel such as coal near the Endoflame will cause it to be consumed by the flower and generate mana
kubejs.ponder.endoflame.text_3:
The flower will consume most furnace fuel in a 7x7 square, centered on itself
(Consumption sped up for demonstration)
kubejs.ponder.endoflame.text_4: To use a mana generating flower, it must be connected to a mana spreader
kubejs.ponder.endoflame.text_5: Either place the flower near an existing spreader...
kubejs.ponder.endoflame.text_6: ...or link it manually with a Wand of the Forest
kubejs.ponder.endoflame_decay.text_1:
§cEntropy comes for all. 
§rThese flowers cannot handle the stress of generating mana forever.
kubejs.ponder.endoflame_decay.text_2: After enough time has passed and enough mana has been generated...
kubejs.ponder.endoflame_decay.text_4: It will crumble into a pile of mush and some other items.
kubejs.ponder.endoflame_decay.text_5: A block can also get left behind where the flower once stood.
kubejs.ponder.endoflame_decay.text_6:
You will need the mush for progression.
Better automate flower production!
kubejs.ponder.entropinnyum.text_1: This is an Entropinnyum, one of the many mana generating flowers
kubejs.ponder.entropinnyum.text_2: It generates sizeable chunks of mana by absorbing TNT explosions
kubejs.ponder.entropinnyum.text_3: TNT generated from a duplicator machine will function, but yield far less mana.
kubejs.ponder.entropinnyum.text_4: It will §cNOT§r absorb the explosion if its mana buffer is not empty!
kubejs.ponder.entropinnyum.text_5: To use a mana generating flower, it must be connected to a mana spreader
kubejs.ponder.entropinnyum.text_6: Either place the flower near an existing spreader...

kubejs.ponder.entropinnyum_decay.text_7: I sure hope you got something to shut off the flow of primed tnt when that happens.
kubejs.ponder.fel_pumpkin.text_1: The Fel Pumpkin can help you get a reliable supply of blaze powder even without a fortress available.
kubejs.ponder.fel_pumpkin.text_2: To use it, place it on top of two iron bars, in the same way you would build a snowman.
kubejs.ponder.fel_pumpkin.text_3: A blaze will spawn. But it is not an ordinary blaze.
kubejs.ponder.fel_pumpkin.text_4: It won't drop blaze rods, but a handful of blaze powder.
kubejs.ponder.fel_pumpkin.text_5: Blazes from fel pumpkins can be used for blaze burners as usual.
kubejs.ponder.gourmaryllis.text_1: This is a Gourmaryllis, one of the many mana generating flowers
kubejs.ponder.gourmaryllis.text_2: It generates mana by consuming food items dropped within a block of it.
kubejs.ponder.gourmaryllis.text_3:
The more nutritious a food is, the longer it takes to digest.
However, the generated mana scales up exponentially.
kubejs.ponder.gourmaryllis.text_4:
Only a single item at a time can be digested.
Any more food in the meantime
§cwill be wasted.
kubejs.ponder.gourmaryllis.text_5: Variety is key. The more varied the foods are, the more mana it will produce, capping out at 8 different foods.
kubejs.ponder.gourmaryllis.text_6: However, using the same food multiple times in a row slows digestion and gives severely diminishing returns.
kubejs.ponder.gourmaryllis.text_7: To use a mana generating flower, it must be connected to a mana spreader
kubejs.ponder.gourmaryllis.text_8: Either place the flower near an existing spreader...
kubejs.ponder.gourmaryllis.text_9: ...or link it manually with a Wand of the Forest

§cEntropy comes for all.

kubejs.ponder.gourmaryllis_decay.text_2: After enough time has passed and enough mana has been generated...
kubejs.ponder.gourmaryllis_decay.text_4: It will crumble into a pile of mush and some other items.

The Growth Accelerator is a device that can speed up certain processes.
To use it, it must be powered by an ME network.
It will only accept connections from the faces marked with a cross.
The Accelerator will affect blocks adjacent to the unmarked faces.
Its intended purpose is to speed up the growth of crystals from budding certus blocks...
Note: Effect sped up for demonstration purposes.
It can also speed up the growth of many crops...
Normally, that would be it. However, in this world, a lot more things will respond to the Accelerator.
It can accelerate the recrystallization of some chemicals.
It can accelerate the decomposition of organic compost into rich soil.
It can then accelerate the actual rich soil!
Accelerated dripstone can do more than just this.
It has a ponder too, anything that involves waiting, can be accelerated!
kubejs.ponder.hydroangeas.text_1: This is a Hydroangeas, one of the many mana generating flowers
kubejs.ponder.hydroangeas.text_2: It generates small amounts of mana by absorbing source water blocks around it.
kubejs.ponder.hydroangeas.text_3: Rainy weather can speed up the production rate, but it is still meager.
kubejs.ponder.hydroangeas.text_4: To use a mana generating flower, it must be connected to a mana spreader
kubejs.ponder.hydroangeas.text_5: Either place the flower near an existing spreader...

kubejs.ponder.hydroangeas_decay.text_7: Note: The normal 3-day decay timer of the hydroangeas is disabled here.
kubejs.ponder.ie_hammah.text_1: The Engineer's Hammer is one of the most important tools when working with Immersive Engineering,
kubejs.ponder.ie_hammah.text_2: The hammer can be used to rotate many blocks.
kubejs.ponder.ie_hammah.text_3: The hammer can be also used to configure certain blocks.
kubejs.ponder.ie_hammah.text_4: For example, right-clicking a side of an accumulator, will set whether it's an input, an output, or neither.
kubejs.ponder.ie_hammah.text_5: Tip: Shift-Right clicking will set the opposite side, if available!
kubejs.ponder.ie_multiblock_assembly.tex: The hammer is needed to assemble Immersive Engineering's multiblocks.
First, build the multiblock. Follow the instructions in the Engineer's manual, or use the Multiblock Projector.
Once the multiblock is built, right click the correct block with the hammer.
The correct block is highlighted in the manual.
If the multiblock is built incorrectly, nothing happens instead.
kubejs.ponder.lava_farming_bucket.text_1: Placing dripstone like this will start dripping lava into the cauldron.
kubejs.ponder.lava_farming_bucket.text_2: After some time, the cauldron will fill up with lava, without consuming the source block!
kubejs.ponder.lava_farming_bucket.text_3: The lava can be withdrawn with a bucket...
kubejs.ponder.lava_farming_bucket.text_5: The same process can be performed with water, but the cauldron fills up gradually instead.
kubejs.ponder.lava_farming_cauldron.head: Farming Lava with Dripstone
kubejs.ponder.lava_farming_cauldron.text: Placing dripstone like this will start dripping lava into the cauldron.
After some time, the cauldron will fill up with lava, without consuming the source block!
The lava can be withdrawn with a bucket...
The same process can be performed with water, but the cauldron fills up gradually instead.
kubejs.ponder.luminar_salt.text_1: When luminar salt is placed in contact with a light source...
kubejs.ponder.luminar_salt.text_3: Removing the light source will de-illuminate the blocks shortly after.
kubejs.ponder.luminar_salt.text_4: The illumination spreads by direct contact, for an amount of blocks based on the source's light level (One less than the light's level).
kubejs.ponder.luminar_salt.text_5: A comparator will emit a redstone signal based on the illumination level, which is NOT the light level.
kubejs.ponder.luminar_salt.text_6: The illumination level is the source's light level minus the amount of salt blocks in between.
kubejs.ponder.luminar_signal_decay.text_: A lone salt block will de-illuminate immediately once the light source is cut.
Something interesting happens if illuminated salt blocks are adjacent...
The salt blocks will piggyback off eachother, creating a comparator output that gradually diminishes over the course of a few ticks!
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_1: The mana enchanter is a structure that lets you copy enchantments from books to items.
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_10: Then, drop enchanted books near the enchanter with the enchants you want to copy onto the item.
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_11: To start enchanting, use the wand of the forest on the enchanter
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_12: The enchanter is active! The books can be now be retrieved.
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_13: However, the item on the enchanter cannot be removed.
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_14: The enchanter must now receive mana...a lot of it.
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_15: This can take a while. Either use faster spreader setups, or ideally, sparks.
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_16: Finally, you can retrieve the enchanted item.
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_17: If at any point, a part of the structure is removed...
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_2: Start with this pattern of obsidian
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_3: Then, add 10 mystical flowers in these spots. Any mystical flower will do.
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_4: Note: The vivid grass is just for visuals, the actual blocks underneath do not matter.
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_5: Add 6 Mana Pylons on top of the outer flowers.
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_6: Finally, a Block of Lapis Lazuli, in the middle
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_7: To form the Enchanter, use a Wand of the Forest on the lapis block
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_8: Use the item you want to enchant on the enchanter block.
kubejs.ponder.mana_enchanter.text_9: The item must not be already enchanted. Curses count as enchants.
kubejs.ponder.mud_drying.text_1: Mud can be slowly dried by placing it on a block that has dripstone hanging underneath.
kubejs.ponder.mud_drying.text_2: Doing so will turn it into clay!
kubejs.ponder.munchdew.text_1: This is a Munchdew, one of the many mana generating flowers
kubejs.ponder.munchdew.text_2:
It generates mana by devouring any leaves in a
17x16x17 cube at a rate of 5 blocks per second.
kubejs.ponder.munchdew.text_3: Once it misses a chance to eat, it will stop and enter a 80s cooldown.
kubejs.ponder.munchdew.text_4: To use a mana generating flower, it must be connected to a mana spreader
kubejs.ponder.munchdew.text_5: Either place the flower near an existing spreader...
kubejs.ponder.munchdew.text_6: ...or link it manually with a Wand of the Forest
kubejs.ponder.munchdew_decay.text_1:
§cEntropy comes for all. 
§rThese flowers cannot handle the stress of generating mana forever.
kubejs.ponder.munchdew_decay.text_2: After enough time has passed and enough mana has been generated...
kubejs.ponder.munchdew_decay.text_4: It will crumble into a pile of mush and some other items.
kubejs.ponder.munchdew_decay.text_5: A block can also get left behind where the flower once stood.
kubejs.ponder.munchdew_decay.text_6:
You will need the mush for progression.
Better automate flower production!
kubejs.ponder.narslimmus.text_1: This is a Narslimmus, one of the many mana generating flowers
kubejs.ponder.narslimmus.text_2: It generates mana by absorbing any slime mobs that wander within 2 blocks of the flower
kubejs.ponder.narslimmus.text_3: Larger slimes will produce more mana.
kubejs.ponder.narslimmus.text_4: The slime must be naturally spawned. Use the slime in a bottle to find a suitable location.
kubejs.ponder.narslimmus.text_5: To use a mana generating flower, it must be connected to a mana spreader
kubejs.ponder.narslimmus.text_6: Either place the flower near an existing spreader...
kubejs.ponder.narslimmus.text_7: ...or link it manually with a Wand of the Forest

kubejs.ponder.nephrite_diode.text_1: The nephrite diode can transfer XP between carved nephrite blocks.
kubejs.ponder.nephrite_diode.text_2: A redstone pulse will transfer one XP point between blocks in the direction of the arrow.
kubejs.ponder.nephrite_fountain.text_1: The nephrite fountain can convert the charge in carved nephrite back to XP orbs.
kubejs.ponder.nephrite_fountain.text_2: To open it, give it a redstone signal.
kubejs.ponder.nephrite_siphon.text_1: The Nephrite Siphon absorbs XP and deposits it in adjacent carved nephrite blocks
kubejs.ponder.nephrite_siphon.text_2: It can absorb XP from players. Crouching will speed up the transfer significantly.
kubejs.ponder.nephrite_siphon.text_3: It can also absorb nearby XP orbs directly.
kubejs.ponder.pure_daisy.text_1: This is a Pure Daisy it is a Functional Flower that changes blocks or fluids placed around it
kubejs.ponder.pure_daisy.text_2: Now we wait for a short period of time and the smooth stone should be changed into livingrock
kubejs.ponder.red_string_basics.text_1: Red Stringed blocks have the capacity to create an ethereal link to another block.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_basics.text_10: Unless you target the red dot face, or its opposite. Then it will flip around
kubejs.ponder.red_string_basics.text_11: Holding the wand of the forest and looking at the red stringed block will highlight its target
kubejs.ponder.red_string_basics.text_2: Each red stringed block connects to a specific category of blocks.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_basics.text_3: The connection starts from the face with the red dot and goes in a straight line.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_basics.text_4: Additionally, the target must be within 8 blocks of the red stringed block.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_basics.text_5: Normally, the link is invisible. To see it in-world, hold a wand of the forest.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_basics.text_6: The red string link can pass through other blocks.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_basics.text_7: Red stringed blocks themselves CANNOT be a target.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_basics.text_8: This means you can create a line of blocks all connected to the same target.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_basics.text_9: Using the wand of the forest while crouching, will rotate the block by 90 degrees on the axis of the targeted face.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_comparator.head: Remote Reading
kubejs.ponder.red_string_comparator.text: The basics of red string linking are covered in the Red String's ponder
If you haven't already, make sure you check that out first.
The Red Stringed Comparator connects to most blocks that can be interfaced with by a redstone comparator.
A comparator reading from the red stringed block will give the same signal strength as one reading directly from the block
kubejs.ponder.red_string_container.text_: The basics of red string linking are covered in the Red String's ponder
If you haven't already, make sure you check that out first.
The Red Stringed Container connects to most blocks that can hold items.
It then acts as if it was said container, allowing for automated input...
When interfacing with blocks that have sided input/output, like furnaces, the side of the red stringed container is used and respected.
Despite the connection being made to the side, the wood is in the top slot, since it was inserted through the top of the container.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_dispenser.text_: The basics of red string linking are covered in the Red String's ponder
If you haven't already, make sure you check that out first.
The Red Stringed Dispenser is a specialized variant of the Red Stringed Container.
It only connects to dispensers and droppers.
Like the container, it allows inserting and extracting items from the connected block
Applying a redstone signal will activate the connected dispenser/dropper
kubejs.ponder.red_string_fertilizer.head: Remote Bonemealing
kubejs.ponder.red_string_fertilizer.text: The basics of red string linking are covered in the Red String's ponder
If you haven't already, make sure you check that out first.
The Red Stringed Nutrifier connects to blocks that can receive bone meal, such as crops and saplings.
Using bone meal on the nutrifier, will instead apply it to the linked block.
The application of bone meal can also be done by dispensers, or deployers.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_interceptor.tex: The basics of red string linking are covered in the Red String's ponder
If you haven't already, make sure you check that out first.
The Red Stringed Interceptor connects to...'Any sufficiently complex block'
In practice, it means blocks that can be interacted with by players.
The interceptor will emit a redstone pulse whenever the target block is right-clicked.
The interaction doesn't necessarily have to be from a player. Deployers can also trigger it.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_relay.text_1: The basics of red string linking are covered in the Red String's ponder
kubejs.ponder.red_string_relay.text_10: Multiple spoofers can link to the same target, each one carrying its own flower. This allows layering the effects in a single position.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_relay.text_2: If you haven't already, make sure you check that out first.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_relay.text_3: The Red Stringed Spoofer is arguably the most complex of the bunch.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_relay.text_4: It targets most mundane flowers, mushrooms and simple mystical flowers. The target can be in a flower pot.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_relay.text_5: Floating, functional or generating flowers are NOT valid targets.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_relay.text_6: To use the spoofer, place a functional or generating flower on top of it.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_relay.text_7: The spoofed flower will now (mostly) act as if it was in the position of the target.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_relay.text_8: That log would have been outside the range of the endoflame, but it is within range of the spoofed position.
kubejs.ponder.red_string_relay.text_9: Note: Mana input/output and item input for functional flowers is still done at the original position.
kubejs.ponder.respawn_anchor.text_1: This is a Respawn Anchor. It allows you to set your respawn point.
kubejs.ponder.respawn_anchor.text_2: To use it, simply right click it with a block of glowstone.
kubejs.ponder.respawn_anchor.text_3: In total, it'll hold 4 charges, meaning 4 glowstone blocks.
kubejs.ponder.respawn_anchor.text_4: Upon respawn, the Respawn anchor will lose one charge.
kubejs.ponder.respawn_anchor.text_5: You can see how many charges remain in this here circle.
kubejs.ponder.respawn_anchor.text_6: You can add glowstone autonomously via a dispenser facing the Respawn Anchor.
kubejs.ponder.respawn_anchor.text_7: And you may either use a comparator to calculate how many uses the Anchor has...
kubejs.ponder.respawn_anchor.text_8: ...or you may use an observer to emit a pulse whenever you respawn.
kubejs.ponder.respawn_anchor.text_9: Oh, and don't worry about beds. §cTrust me.§r
kubejs.ponder.rosa_arcana.text_1: This is a Rosa Arcana, one of the many mana generating flowers
kubejs.ponder.rosa_arcana.text_2: It generates mana from experience. It will drain XP from players standing next to it.
kubejs.ponder.rosa_arcana.text_3: It will also absorb any experience orb within one block of itself.
kubejs.ponder.rosa_arcana.text_4: Enchanted items dropped near it will have the enchantments stripped from them and turned into xp orbs, like with a grindstone. Does not affect curses.
kubejs.ponder.rosa_arcana.text_5: To use a mana generating flower, it must be connected to a mana spreader
kubejs.ponder.rosa_arcana.text_6: Either place the flower near an existing spreader...
kubejs.ponder.rosa_arcana.text_7: ...or link it manually with a Wand of the Forest

kubejs.ponder.rosa_arcana_decay.text_7: If the enchanter block appears outside of a valid structure, you have one tick of time...
kubejs.ponder.stone_generator.text_1: Although more intricate, you may also want to build a Stone Generator.
kubejs.ponder.stone_generator.text_10:
Oh, and stone can be mined faster than cobblestone.
§cDo keep this in mind.§r
kubejs.ponder.stone_generator.text_2: While a Cobblestone Generator works by flowing lava next to water...
kubejs.ponder.stone_generator.text_3: A Stone Generator works by flowing lava ON TOP of water.
kubejs.ponder.stone_generator.text_4: Something else to note is that, once placed, lava doesn't flow upon neccesity. It ALWAYS tries to flow whenever possible.
kubejs.ponder.stone_generator.text_5: This is known as the "Global Timer".
kubejs.ponder.stone_generator.text_6: "Why is this important?" you may ask.
kubejs.ponder.stone_generator.text_7: If you break the stone block at the wrong time...
kubejs.ponder.stone_generator.text_9: ...resulting in the creation of cobblestone instead.
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_1: This is a Thermalily, one of the many mana generating flowers
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_10: The comparator signal does NOT tick down. It is up to the player to figure out how to use this value to delay the next lava block.
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_11: The thermalily can only absorb one block of lava at a time.
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_12: If you try to place more lava while it's generating or on cooldown...
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_13: To use a mana generating flower, it must be connected to a mana spreader
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_14: Either place the flower near an existing spreader...
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_15: ...or link it manually with a Wand of the Forest
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_2: It generates a lot of mana by absorbing nearby lava source blocks.
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_3: After absorbing lava, it will generate mana for about 45 seconds.
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_4: When it stops generating mana, it will enter a cooldown period.
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_5: The cooldown can vary from 20 seconds to 5 whole minutes
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_6: The cooldown can be read with a comparator.
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_7: The comparator output is off only while generating mana
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_8: When the cooldown starts, the comparator outputs a signal based on the length
kubejs.ponder.thermalily.text_9: The signal strength grows by 1 for every 20 seconds of cooldown

kubejs.ponder.yeast_culture.text_1: Yeast Culture can be propagated into water. To do so, place them next to eachother.
kubejs.ponder.yeast_culture.text_2: Then, drop sugar into the yeast culture. NOT in the water.
kubejs.ponder.yeast_culture.text_4: In order for yeast culture to do its thing, it must receive a block update.
kubejs.ponder.yeast_culture.text_5: In other words, pretend it's an Observer.
kubejs.ponder.yeast_culture.text_6: The sugar gets consumed, and the water turns into more yeast culture!
kubejs.ponder.yeast_culture.text_7: The new culture can now be removed and replaced with more water.
kubejs.ponder.yeast_culture.text_8: Tip: A redstone lamp connected to a timer can provide block updates.
